title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Wall Street closed the week higher (S&P +0.5%, Nasdaq +0.9%, Dow +0.5%, its first winning week in three) despite a soft Friday, after Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks pushed September rate-hike odds to ~60% (from 35%), lifted 2-yr Treasury yields to 4.35%, and sent gold down >3%; markets are closed over the weekend with no fresh moves since
Markets: Focus shifts to next week — Broadcom, Palo Alto Networks, Dell and HPE report earnings, and the August jobs report lands Friday, Sept. 4

Companies: Chevron and Halliburton are nearing deals to expand Venezuelan oil operations, with Exxon and ConocoPhillips also evaluating access to fields holding an estimated 90B barrels in reserves, as the US negotiates a stake in a joint venture and Venezuela agrees to redirect roughly $2.8B of crude exports from China to the US
Companies: Shein is set to price its Hong Kong IPO Aug. 31 (shares trading Sept. 1), seeking up to ~$1.77B at a valuation well below the $64B it commanded in 2023-24 private rounds

Macro/Policy: A 9th Circuit ruling against Kalshi (affirming states can regulate prediction markets as gambling) conflicts with an earlier 3rd Circuit decision favoring CFTC oversight, teeing up a likely Supreme Court fight over the industry
Macro/Policy: Warsh's Jackson Hole comments signaled the Fed isn't convinced underlying inflation has improved, keeping a September hike squarely in play ahead of next week's jobs data
